abstract: A small number of mouse embryos and embryonal carcinoma cells were pressed by mica sheet; then the extruded DNA complexes were adsorbed to mica and processed for electron microscopy. Extrachromosomal circular DNA complexes longer than 1 μm emerged during the compaction process of mouse embryos and during the differentiation of embryonal carcinoma cells induced with retinoic acid. These DNA molecules are discussed as possible products of developmental gene rearrangements occurring in the chromosomal DNA.
abstract_ja: マウス胚と胎児性癌細胞の少数の試料をマイカシートで圧迫し、押し出されたDNA複合体をマイカに吸着させて電子顕微鏡で観察した。胚の圧縮過程およびレチノイン酸で誘導した胎児性癌細胞の分化過程で、1μmを超える染色体外環状DNA複合体が出現した。これらのDNA分子は、染色体DNAにおいて発生時に起こる遺伝子再配列の産物である可能性があると考察される。
